display: Year 3 primary teacher in Auckland with a multicultural, high-ESOL class. Happy to talk about newcomer support and classroom practice.

signals.text: I'm looking for ways to help a newcomer child who understands a lot but isn't speaking yet, especially a Mandarin-speaking child.
My school has no Mandarin-speaking teacher aide this term because the ESOL budget was cut.
I'm hunting for relief funding, grants or volunteers that can cover ESOL language support in a state primary.
I'd love a Mandarin or Korean speaker who could check the pronunciation on my newcomer picture cards.
My newcomer buddy system works for Samoan and Hindi but not yet for Korean or Mandarin.
Parents have asked about a homework club, but I have no time to run one myself.
I'm worn out. I got sick twice this term and still came in, so the holidays can't come soon enough.
My old villa has leaky windows, and the back-window replacement has slipped to mid-November.
I'd like trustworthy advice on dealing with builders who keep changing schedules and scope.
I worry I'm not doing enough for the quiet kids who are still finding their feet.
My dad just had a hip replacement and is pushing himself too hard, so I'm helping my parents with recovery.
I want to bring a bit of the old fun back to my Thursday-night netball. My knees are complaining.

offers.text: Eight years of primary teaching, four of them with a high-ESOL class of kids from about fourteen countries.
A set of about 200 hand-drawn picture cards for newcomers, and I can share how I design and use them.
A working newcomer buddy system (older same-language buddies) that I can describe step by step so other schools can copy it.
A class blog that parents actually read, and I can share what makes it work.
Basic te reo Māori and some Samoan classroom phrases, plus practical tips for welcoming Pasifika and Māori families.
Classroom-level feedback and testing for ESOL, language-learning or children's-literacy tools, without sharing any child's identity.
A teacher's view of what a Year 3 newcomer needs in the first weeks, useful for researchers, app makers or community groups.
Experience living through a 1920s villa window renovation in Auckland, and I can share what I've learned about leaks and the schedule.

catchers.hypo: Hi, I'm a Mandarin-speaking university student in Auckland. I'd like to volunteer a couple of hours a week helping a primary school with a newly arrived Chinese child.
catchers.can: I can raise it with the principal so the school can arrange a safe, approved volunteer placement. I can also share my picture cards so the volunteer knows what to start with.
catchers.confirm: Are you happy to go through the school's usual volunteer approval process, including any police vetting, before meeting children?

catchers.hypo: I run a small charity that funds language support for refugee and migrant children in West Auckland schools.
catchers.can: I can pass your details to my principal, who is already looking at relief funds for ESOL support. I can describe what kind of help a high-ESOL class could use.
catchers.confirm: Does your funding cover state primary schools, and in particular a Mandarin-language aide?

catchers.hypo: I'm a developer building a picture-and-pronunciation tool for children who are just starting English. Could a teacher look at the idea?
catchers.can: I can give honest classroom feedback and compare it with how my hand-drawn picture cards work. I won't share any child's identity or photos.
catchers.confirm: Does your tool need only general teacher feedback, with no access to children's names, photos or class data?

catchers.hypo: I'm a teacher at a school in another city. How did you set up buddies who speak the same language as a new student?
catchers.can: I can share the buddy-system steps, what works for Samoan and Hindi, and the gaps I still have. I'm also keen to swap ideas for languages where there's no buddy.
catchers.confirm: Are you a teacher or school leader looking to set up or improve a newcomer-buddy scheme?

catchers.hypo: I'm an orthopaedic physio who volunteers advice for older people after hip replacements. A friend said you might know someone who needs it.
catchers.can: I can pass your offer to my mum, who is looking after my dad after his hip replacement at home. I can ask whether they'd want a call.
catchers.confirm: Are you a registered physiotherapist who can give general recovery advice to a family in the Papakura area?

catchers.hypo: I'm a builder or window specialist in Auckland who does honest, fixed-price quotes on old villas. Do you know anyone with leaky windows?
catchers.can: I can pass your name to my partner Ben, who is a plumber's apprentice and manages our villa project. We could compare notes on windows and schedules.
catchers.confirm: Do you do fixed-price work on 1920s timber villas in central or south Auckland, with a written schedule?

catchers.hypo: I help set up after-school homework clubs run by volunteers. A parent group at one school wants one but has no staff.
catchers.can: I can introduce the idea to my principal, since parents at my school have asked for one too. I can't run it myself because I have no spare weekday evenings.
catchers.confirm: Can your homework club run entirely on volunteers or parents, without needing a teacher to staff it?

catchers.hypo: I'm a speech-language therapist working with bilingual kids. When a newcomer child goes silent, is it shyness or something else?
catchers.can: I can share what I observe in the classroom in general terms and what picture-based communication has worked. I'm keen to learn the signs to watch for.
catchers.confirm: Can you offer general guidance on silent-period behaviour without needing to identify any individual child?

forbids.text: I won't share any child's name, photo, family details or anything that could identify them. Those stay inside the school system.
I can't take on weekday evening commitments during term.
I can't run anything in the school day, because my lunch hour goes on class admin.
I can't spend more than about $50 a term of my own money on school resources.
I won't discuss my family's personal finances.

projects.name: Newcomer buddy system
projects.text: Pairing each new child with an older buddy who speaks the same language. It works for Samoan and Hindi, but there's no Mandarin buddy yet and Korean doesn't work yet.

policy.t1: Constraints on school resourcing, term dates and what kind of help the school and I can use, plus general villa-renovation questions.
policy.t2: Personal worries about individual children (never identified) and my workload and health, and family health matters once I trust the person.
policy.never: Children's identities, names and photos, my family's finances, and my villa budget.
